answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with decay. In an agent economy, each identity must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and its reputation grows only from completed, peer-attested work - like tending a garden, where a knoll of trust builds slowly, and a single comet of flashy activity cannot fake it. An attacker must fund every fake identity separately, and slashing burns the deposit of any identity caught cheating, so thousands of sock puppets cost thousands of deposits with no reputation gained. Honest agents pay once; attackers pay per identity, forever.
